A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca-activated tension in skinned skeletal muscle fibers is controlled by the concentration of free Mg-ATP in solution, the concentration of Ca, and the temperature.
the Ca sensitivity of the tension response is controlled by the ratio of the rate constants for the attachment of Ca to the thin-filament regulatory sites and the detachment of Ca from these sites.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the tension of skinned muscle fibers can be controlled by Ca-activated force generation and by the Mg-ATP concentration.
Ca-activated tension in skinned skeletal muscle fibers is controlled by the ratio of the concentrations of Ca-bound regulatory proteins to Ca-bound actomyosin.
skinned fibers are regulated by the same mechanisms as intact fibers, but the regulation is more easily studied in the skinned fibers.
